clue.text: It's no business of the pedestrian

definitions.text: It's no business of the pedestrian

parts.words: It's no business of the pedestrian
parts.note: trade from customers who arrive in their own coaches, rather than on foot, is the custom no walker brings

explanation.surface: A remark that walkers have no stake in commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: The trade meant is the custom of the rich, who once came to shops in their own coaches; a pedestrian, arriving on foot, by definition brings none of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names wealthy custom, historically from people driven in coaches, so walkers are excluded from it.

clue.text: Event in the flat part of England

explanation.surface: A happening in the low-lying region of England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Flat is British flat racing, without jumps; this is also the name of a handicap race run at Newmarket, and of the fenland county.
explanation.definitionFit: A Newmarket handicap horse race is one sense; the eastern county containing Cambridge is the other.

clue.text: Mole's associate brought to book

parts.note: the friend of Mole in The Wind in the Willows is a character in a book, not a culprit caught

explanation.surface: A spy's contact has been caught and punished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought to book' looks like punishment, but it means put in a novel: Kenneth Grahame's The Wind in the Willows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Water Rat, Mole's friend in Grahame's novel, is known by this nickname, which also means irritable.

clue.text: Shun income got by collecting flies

indicators.note: collecting gathers the letters together and reassembles them in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone avoids earnings that come from gathering things.
explanation.definitionFit: Parasitic wasps, often called by this name plus the word fly, lay eggs in other insects.

clue.text: Might "Il Trovatore' bring joy to the island?

parts.note: glee means joy
the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A question whether Verdi's opera might cheer an island audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Il Trovatore' is Italian for the troubadour, so here it names a medieval minstrel rather than the opera.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval minstrel or singer of songs, as a troubadour was.

clue.text: They examine layout of streets

indicators.note: a layout is an arrangement, so the letters of streets are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Inspectors check how roads are planned.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspectors who try things out are people who examine.

clue.text: Sacred river seen in aerial photograph

indicators.note: seen in means the letters can be found inside these words

explanation.surface: A holy river appears in an aerial picture.
explanation.walkthrough: In Coleridge's Kubla Khan, 'Alph, the sacred river, ran'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge names the holy river of Xanadu in his poem Kubla Khan.

clue.text: Men left me out in revision of pay

indicators.note: revision reworks things, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: In a pay review, the men left me out.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal word for salary or fees received for work.

clue.text: Ordinary choice between follower of Clapham and the school of Epicurus

parts.note: Clapham Common is a London park, so the word that follows Clapham is common
or offers a choice between things
Epicurus taught in his Garden in Athens, which gave his school its name

explanation.surface: An everyday choice between a south London man and Greek philosophy.
explanation.walkthrough: Clapham is a district of south London famous for its Common, a large public park.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for something plain, everyday and unremarkable.

clue.text: There's nothing to beat being single!

explanation.surface: A cheerful boast that unmarried life is the best.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word: without a match, that is, with no partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Unequalled, peerless things have nothing to beat them; someone with no partner or spouse is literally lacking a match.

clue.text: Poor disturbance held against Dutch anarchist

indicators.note: the jumbled letters hold the next piece inside them
a disturbance stirs things up, so the letters of poor are jumbled

parts.note: V, short for versus, means against

explanation.surface: A Dutch radical charged with causing a poor riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbance' rearranges POOR into PROO, and 'held' puts V inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Provos were a 1960s Amsterdam anarchist protest movement, and a member was called by that name.

clue.text: Paul is a good one to call

definitions.text: Paul is a good one to call

parts.words: Paul is a good one to call
parts.note: the name Paul ends with the same sound as the word call, so it pairs with it in verse

explanation.surface: A tip that Paul is a reliable person to telephone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'call' looks like a verb meaning telephone, but it is the word that Paul chimes with in a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Words with matching end sounds, as Paul and call have, are what poets pair at line ends.

clue.text: Consider withdrawing this reward

indicators.note: withdrawing means drawing back, so the word for consider is read backwards

parts.note: to deem is to consider or judge

explanation.surface: Think about taking this prize back.
explanation.definitionFit: An old poetic word for a deserved recompense or due wage.

clue.text: Broke a mug one of Mariana's you say?

indicators.note: a broken mug is in pieces, so the letters of a mug are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone smashed a mug belonging to a woman called Mariana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mariana's, you say' is the Marianas spoken: the Pacific island chain to which this island belongs.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the largest island in the Mariana chain in the western Pacific.

clue.text: Include a particle of pity

parts.note: to compass is to encompass or include
an ion is a charged particle

explanation.surface: Add a little sympathy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sympathy for suffering is a near synonym of both words.

clue.text: They don't sneak empty bottles

explanation.surface: Some people who won't tell tales, and some drained bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense comes from the saying that the departed tell no tales, so they never inform.
explanation.definitionFit: Corpses tell no tales, so they never inform; drinkers' slang calls drained wine bottles by the same phrase.

clue.text: Making a pretence of moving

explanation.surface: Faking being emotional.
explanation.definitionFit: To feign something is to put it on as a show; a touching scene stirs the emotions.

clue.text: Hold, say, floating votes in the end

indicators.note: the end means the following word is placed at the finish
floating suggests drifting loose, so the letters of votes are moved about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A ship's hold, perhaps, or uncommitted ballots at the finish of a poll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold, say' is the definition by sound: spoken, it is 'holed'. 'floating' rearranges VOTES into STOVE, and 'the end' puts IN after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hull smashed inwards has been holed, which is how the spoken word 'hold' sounds.

clue.text: Foreign title you got for noble deeds initially, I hear

indicators.note: I hear means the letters are spoken as their names
the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the first letters of for, noble and deeds are F, N and D

explanation.surface: A knighthood from abroad awarded for gallantry, by report.
explanation.walkthrough: Say the three letters' names, eff-en-dee, and you have the title.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Turkish honorific for a man of education or standing, a title from abroad to English speakers.

clue.text: Forbidden? This still is

parts.note: still is a distilling apparatus: a moonshiner's one is unlawful

explanation.surface: A question whether something is still banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like an adverb meaning yet, but it is a distilling apparatus, which makes whisky unlawfully when unlicensed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unlawful is forbidden, as an unlicensed whisky still is.

clue.text: He promises better success

parts.note: read better as one who bets: a racing adviser promises punters winners

explanation.surface: A man pledging an improved result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' looks like the comparative of good, but it is a person who places bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing adviser sells punters forecasts of which horses will win.

clue.text: In the late 17th century Halifax was said to be tidier

definitions.text: In the late 17th century Halifax was said to be

explanation.surface: A historical note on a statesman's reputation for neatness.
explanation.walkthrough: George Savile, Marquess of Halifax, wrote The Character of a Trimmer and was known by the nickname: one who shifts between parties.
explanation.definitionFit: A politician who changes sides to keep balance was Halifax's nickname; neater is the comparative sense.

clue.text: Wine to give to uncle

explanation.surface: Handing a bottle to a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old slang for a pawnbroker, so giving something to uncle means pawning it.
explanation.definitionFit: A German white from the Rhine is one sense; to pawn goods with a pawnbroker is the other.

clue.text: Bail out in South of France

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Securing someone's release on bail in the south of France.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a cathedral town in the Tarn, in southern France.

clue.text: Guitry has trouble about bill

indicators.note: about means going round the next piece
trouble means disorder, so the letters of has are shuffled

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: A man named Guitry is in difficulty over an invoice.
explanation.walkthrough: Sacha Guitry was a French actor and playwright. 'trouble' shuffles HAS into SHA, and 'about' puts AC around inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Guitry was the surname of the French dramatist whose first name this is.

clue.text: About to put up "de luxe food

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: to set is to put

explanation.surface: About to serve luxury dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for choice delicacies or dainties.

clue.text: This string will hardly do

parts.note: put this word before string and you get a meagre budget that barely suffices

explanation.surface: A complaint that a piece of cord is not good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: Doing something on a budget so tiny it barely suffices is doing it on this word plus string.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwear that ties with laces, joined to string, makes the phrase for a barely adequate budget.

clue.text: Third of Germany dominated by Hitler

definitions.text: Third of Germany dominated by Hitler

parts.words: Third of Germany dominated by Hitler
parts.note: the Nazi state was called the Third empire of the Germans

explanation.surface: A fraction of Germany under Hitler's control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Third' looks like a fraction, but it is the ordinal in the Nazi name for their state.
explanation.definitionFit: The German word for empire, used in the Nazi name for their regime.

clue.text: Sent to gaol for what was done

explanation.surface: Imprisoned for the deed.
explanation.definitionFit: A court that sends someone to prison has consigned them; a crime carried out has been perpetrated.

clue.text: He exemplifies relatively wide generation gap

definitions.text: He exemplifies relatively wide generation gap

parts.words: He exemplifies relatively wide generation gap
parts.note: relatively means in terms of family: a grandchild's son is three generations below his ancestor

explanation.surface: A man who illustrates a fairly big age divide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relatively' seems to mean fairly, but it means as a relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A male descendant three generations down is separated from his ancestor by a wide family gap.
